clue.text: First and last, putting out ostentatious show of wealth is super hot

indicators.note: putting out is read as stretching something outward around another piece, so the flashy word opens to hold the pair

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery and showy riches
A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A boast that, all things considered, flaunting your riches is very cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and last' is not about letters of a clue word but of the alphabet, A and Z, placed inside BLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blazing is burning fiercely, so extremely hot; a straight synonym.

clue.text: "Chicken Song" by Queen

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a ballad or song
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A title credit: a novelty number called Chicken Song, performed by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Chicken Song' look like a title; 'Chicken' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is a hen kept for its eggs, so a chicken by function.

clue.text: Springer: final letter to American taking drug to "crib"

indicators.note: taking means the outer word takes in, or holds, the other pieces

parts.note: an American calls the last letter of the alphabet zee

indicators.note: to here means the drug is added on after the bed

parts.note: a crib is a child's bed
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Someone who leaps up from the end of the alphabet, prompting an American to take drugs to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: ZEBEDEE is the spring-mounted character in the children's TV show The Magic Roundabout, hence 'Springer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magic Roundabout character bounces about on a coiled spring instead of legs, so he is a literal springer.

clue.text: Zero Mostel, infamously, holding it up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, in reverse
holding means the two clue words contain the letters needed, sitting across the word break

explanation.surface: Remarks on actor Zero Mostel, notorious for propping something up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'Zero' with 'Mostel' as the actor's name; the definition is 'Zero' alone. The letters LIN straddle 'Mostel, infamously' and read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is the score word for nought, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Leaves very quickly brushing off sheep tick burdens

indicators.note: brushing off means flicking something away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to skedaddle is to run off in a hurry
a ked is a bloodsucking parasite of sheep, also called the sheep tick

explanation.surface: Someone bolting from a flock while flicking off parasites that weigh on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burdens' is a verb here: removing KED from SKEDADDLES leaves the verb meaning loads with a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To saddle someone with something is to load them with an unwelcome responsibility.

clue.text: Pole, 40, found in analytical exploration initially

indicators.note: found in means the number sits inside the pair of letters
initially means the first letters of the two words

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A Polish scientist, aged forty, turns up in a piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland; it means a rod. The A and E from 'analytical exploration' wrap the Roman 40.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which wheels turn, a kind of pole.

clue.text: Rob dictator unendingly — I have last to fail

indicators.note: unendingly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a despot is a tyrannical ruler

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tyrant, endlessly, is told he must fail at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To despoil is to plunder or strip of possessions, a synonym of rob.

clue.text: Gene drains liquid I left behind and puts at risk

indicators.note: liquid means fluid, flowing freely, so the letters run into a new order
left behind means the letter I is left out of the shuffled pool

explanation.surface: A genetic procedure that drains fluid and leaves the patient in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' rearranges GENE DRAINS once the I named in 'I left behind' is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to expose to harm, so endangers is a synonym of puts at risk.

clue.text: Willy Wonka's protégé is luckier? Betcha mess it up!

indicators.note: mess it up means jumble the preceding letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast that Wonka's chosen heir got lucky, daring him to blow it.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Wilder played Willy Wonka in the 1971 film, whose young hero takes over the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy who wins the golden ticket in the Roald Dahl story is chosen by Wonka to inherit the factory.

clue.text: Logo to signify minicab "optional" when all empty

indicators.note: when all empty means each of the three words loses its interior, keeping only the outside letters

explanation.surface: A design meant to show that a minicab is an optional extra once everyone is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem standing for a firm, and a symbol is any emblem or sign.

clue.text: Sarcasm from Benny on the way up or down?

definitions.text: on the way up or down?
definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a place on a slope

indicators.note: from here means the sarcasm comes from the comic, whose name goes first

parts.note: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian known for slapstick and saucy sketches
side is taken by the setter as cheek or sarcastic attitude, close to its slang sense of airs and swagger

explanation.surface: A question about whether a comedian's barbed remark came while he was rising or falling.
explanation.walkthrough: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian. Taking 'side' as sarcasm is a stretch: its slang sense is airs or swagger.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of a hill is where a walker is either climbing or descending, so the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: Financial backers of goods: rhinoceros skins

parts.note: produce means things grown or made, goods

indicators.note: skins means the outer layers of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trade line about investors in a market dealing in rhino hides.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Wilder starred in Mel Brooks's film The Producers.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or theatre producer raises the money and backs the show financially.

clue.text: "Comedy hero always looked knowingly youthful," starts White

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of the six quoted words

parts.words: Comedy hero always looked knowingly youthful

explanation.surface: A review quote about a comic lead who always looked wise beyond his years, credited to a critic named White.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' poses as the critic's name but is the definition; the quotation's first letters do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalk is white, so chalky describes a pale, whitish colour.

clue.text: Wilder scientist was described thus in the second person: no good

parts.note: the second-person pronoun is you

explanation.surface: A note that the scientist Gene Wilder played was addressed directly and found useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene Wilder played the scientist in Young Frankenstein, so the film title describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mel Brooks film calls Wilder's mad doctor Young Frankenstein, so that adjective described the scientist.

clue.text: Proper attitude when time has passed for agreed period of exchange

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially correct or proper

indicators.note: has passed means the time letter has gone, leaving the word without it

parts.note: a stance is a stated position or attitude

explanation.surface: Good manners, applied once enough time has gone by, before an agreed swap.
explanation.walkthrough: USANCE is a banking term: the customary time allowed for paying a foreign bill of exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: In trade finance this is the settled length of time allowed before a bill of exchange must be paid.

clue.text: Intellectuals initially like sex both ways, interrupted by hearsay regularly

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of the word
interrupted by means other letters break into the middle

parts.note: IT is a crossword word for sex appeal; both ways gives it forwards then backwards

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Clever people who supposedly enjoy all kinds of sex, though it is mostly rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: From 'hearsay' the even letters give ERA, which breaks into IT TI.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read people of letters, the educated class.

clue.text: Put in chasing group following Italian giants after small loss

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the club

parts.note: Inter is the Milan football club, a giant of Italian football

indicators.note: loss means a letter is taken away

parts.note: a posse is a band pursuing a fugitive

explanation.surface: A cycling picture: the peloton chasing the leaders, behind Italian heavyweights, after a minor setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian giants' is a football club, not big men; 'after small loss' tells you the chasing group sheds an S before it is joined on.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpose is to insert something between, so put in.

clue.text: Pirate's unfettered rage

definitions.meaning: Long John is the one-legged pirate of Treasure Island
rage with its outer letters unchained leaves AG, the chemical symbol for this precious metal

explanation.surface: A buccaneer's furious temper running loose.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: strip the 'fetters' (outer letters) from 'rage' to get AG, the chemical symbol for the metal. With 19, this gives the Gene Wilder film Silver Streak.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirate's surname in Stevenson's novel is also a precious metal, symbol Ag, the core of the word rage.

clue.text: Barely run 22s

parts.note: 22 is the answer to the clue Do better than men in the open, so this means run bare in the open air

explanation.surface: A short note about someone dashing naked outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 22s stands for the answer to 22, plural. With 18, this gives the Gene Wilder film Silver Streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaking is running naked through a public place, typically outdoors for a dare.

clue.text: In frenzy, mescaline brings forth biological catalysts

indicators.note: In means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled frenzy unleashes chemical reactions in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Enzymes are proteins that speed up chemical reactions in living cells.

clue.text: Musical dueller to make support illegal?

parts.note: to make illegal is to ban
a joist is a supporting beam in a floor or ceiling

explanation.surface: A question about whether a musician's duel could make a building's supports unlawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make ... illegal' gives BAN. 'Musical dueller' recalls 'Duelling Banjos' from the film Deliverance.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo player could take part in a duel like the famous banjo-versus-guitar showdown.

clue.text: Do better than men in the open

parts.note: to outdo is to surpass
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, the men

explanation.surface: A challenge to outperform the men in the open air.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor means happening outside, in the fresh air.

clue.text: Wild unknowns bend backwards

indicators.note: backwards means the whole string of letters is read from the end

parts.note: in algebra y and z are unknown quantities
an arc is a curve or bend

explanation.surface: Mystery creatures bending over backwards like contortionists.
explanation.walkthrough: With 26, this gives Stir Crazy, the Gene Wilder and Richard Pryor film.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy and wild both mean frenzied or out of control.

clue.text: Idle around; copy in naked gents — it's unorthodox

indicators.note: around means the name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Eric Idle is a member of Monty Python
CC stands for carbon copy

indicators.note: naked means the word is stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lazy chap hanging about copying naked men: odd behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like an adjective for lazy but is the Monty Python member; 'naked' strips the outer letters of 'gents', and 'around' wraps the name about the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person or idea departs from the usual, conventional way.

clue.text: Annoyed when made permanent, knight goes right in

indicators.note: goes means the knight letter leaves and another comes in to take its place

parts.note: inked means set down in ink, made permanent, as with a tattoo or signed deal
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone irritated when a deal is signed and a knight intervenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Irked means irritated, a straight synonym of annoyed.

clue.text: Can cause trouble

definitions.meaning: to ... is to ... up trouble, to agitate

explanation.surface: An admission that one is capable of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb; it is the noun for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, and to stir is to make mischief by agitating others.

clue.text: Head off gambler with low income heading back to sleeping compartment

indicators.note: heading back means the assembled letters run in the reverse direction
income is read as in plus come, so the cow sound goes in
head off means the first letter of the word is cut away

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler
to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: Fending off a poor gambler before going back to one's railway berth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'income' splits as 'in come', so the cow's sound goes into the beheaded gambler; 'heading back' then reverses the lot, giving ETTEMOOR read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A roomette is a small private sleeping room on an American train.

clue.text: Wilder collaborator runs into reserves

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: to book is to reserve, so books is reserves
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone running into reserves of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel Brooks directed Gene Wilder in The Producers, Blazing Saddles and Young Frankenstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel Brooks wrote and directed several of Gene Wilder's best-known films.

clue.text: Nasty smell with nothing to add, surprise, surprise!

parts.note: BO is body odour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bad pong with nothing more to say about it, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation shouted to startle someone is a way of springing a surprise.

clue.text: Garland's original Eastern holiday

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland; with the 's it reads as leis
ur- is a prefix meaning original or earliest

explanation.surface: Judy Garland's first trip to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garland' poses as Judy Garland's name but means a flower wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work, as a holiday is.

clue.text: Joe receives text your setter would read as "drive illegally"

indicators.note: receives means the name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: yr is text-speak for your
the setter is I, and I would contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Joe receives a message saying what his crossword setter would call stealing a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To joyride is to take a car without permission and drive it recklessly for fun.
